recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a non-substantive source reconciliation matching the Published/Persuasive decision and current rendered output; no broader TOC, page generation, or link-checking change was evidenced.
issue_request: FHIR-38817 was a Published/Persuasive R5 correction for the 2022Sep Table of Contents, where toc.html linked to broken-link.html at section 1.11. The accepted resolution was to fix the tooling/source path so the broken-link page does not show in the ToC or consume a section number.
initial_application: No prior repository commit explicitly mentioned FHIR-38817. The relevant source was introduced by a41e7958c85a2583535192048e11abfbfdf13be4 on 2022-09-08, which added source/broken-link.html, the publish.ini page entry, and a source/hierarchy.xml child under toc.html; the hierarchy child made the page eligible for TOC generation and section numbering.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2022-10-24 state that FHIR-38817 was a tooling change and that the broken-link page is not supposed to be in the TOC. A current check found broken-link.html once in the 2022Sep ballot TOC but zero times in the published R5 TOC and current build.fhir.org TOC, indicating current rendered behavior is correct and the remaining reconciliation is source cleanup.
reconciliation: Removed only the Broken Link Page entry from source/hierarchy.xml. The publish.ini broken-link.html entry and source/broken-link.html were left intact so broken example references can still reach the explanatory page, while the page no longer participates in the source hierarchy that drives TOC and section numbering.
source_changes: source/hierarchy.xml: removed the Broken Link Page child from the Table of Contents hierarchy.
